newsitem.title: USA: Michigan air crash probe focuses on engine.
newsitem.headline: Michigan air crash probe focuses on engine.

text.p: Federal investigators chopped through ice and frozen mud at the Delta Comair crash site on Monday to excavate the commuter plane's engines in search of clues to explain last Thursday's tragedy.
Investigators want to know why cockpit levers indicated that pilots of Comair Flight 3272 apparently took steps to shut down the right engine and activate a fire extinguishing system.
"They'll be looking at that right engine," said National Transportation Safety Board spokesman Paul Schlamm.

NTSB officials said on Sunday they had no indication of an in-flight fire, but the engines of the 30-seat Embraer 120 Brasilia aircraft were buried underground when the plane nosedived at 4,000 feet (1,200 metres) and slammed into a snowy field.

In addition, cockpit controls showed the right propeller had been "feathered" to reduce aerodynamic drag, NTSB board member John Hammerschmidt said on Sunday, adding that controls for the left engine were in normal operating position.
Feathering is a technique of changing the pitch, or angle, of propellor blades to lessen air resistance when an engine is idling or shut off.
Although the propellers had not yet been recovered, wreckage showed evidence that they were rotating at the time of impact, Schlamm said.
The fiery crash in rural Monroe County, Mich., about 25 miles (40 km) south of Detroit Metropolitan Airport, killed 29 people, including three crew members, flying from Cincinnati to Detroit.
Monroe County Medical Examiner David Lieberman said late on Monday that the remains of nearly all of the victims had been identified and were being turned over to their families.

The brother and sister of one of the victims, 31-year-old Gregory Barrow, visited the crash site along with family and friends and on Monday and thanked county volunteers and officials for helping them deal with the tragedy.

"It was good for us to all go out to the crash site. It was just easy not to deal with it, but we all believe the only way that we could start dealing with this is to understand it as much as we could," said Leonard Barrow, who met with reporters along with his sister, Lynda.

The doomed Comair connector flight for Delta Air Lines claimed their younger brother, a law student who was returning to Detroit for his girlfriend's birthday on Thursday after visiting his parents in Florida.
Lynda Barrow said the family received flowers from people who lost loved ones in the 1987 crash of a Northwest Airlines jetliner in Detroit.

Schlamm said the investigators also began to decontaminate and move pieces of wreckage from the crash site into a building at the nearby Monroe County Fairgrounds, where they will try to reconstruct the Brazilian-made Embraer commuter plane.
But frigid weather conditions were making it difficult for workers to extract pieces of the aircraft.
"They have to get through that frozen ground and ice without damaging the wreckage," Schlamm said.

In addition to examining the Pratt & Whitney engines, investigators also were continuing to probe the possibility that icing contributed to the crash. About 20 minutes after the crash, the pilot of a DC-3 aircraft reported icing in the same vicinity.

NTSB officials said they expected to wrap up most on-site work by the end of the week. Hammerschmidt, the lead investigator, returned to Washington, D.C. on Monday, and will direct the probe from there.
